chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever reaches Jam', he has accomplished the Hajj.

And he said: Whichever Muhrim is a Qarin (one who combines Tamattu' and Ifrad), or an Ifradi (one performing exclusive Hajj), or a Mutamatti' (one performing Tamattu'), arrives and has missed the Hajj, so let him free himself from Ihram with Umrah, and upon him is the Hajj in the following year.

He said, and he said regarding a man who catches up with the Imam and he is in Jam', so he said: If he thinks that he will reach 'Arafat, so he will stand in it for a little while, then he will reach Jam' before the emergence of the sun, so let him go to it; and if he thinks that he will not reach it until they depart, so he should not go to it, and let him stay in Jam', so he has completed his Hajj.

key_terms.جَمْع: Jam', the area near Muzdalifah where pilgrims gather after 'Arafat.
key_terms.عَرَفَات: 'Arafat, the plain where the essential standing (wuquf) of Hajj takes place.
key_terms.قَارِن: Qarin, a pilgrim who combines the rites of Tamattu' and Ifrad.
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّع: Mutamatti', a pilgrim performing Tamattu' (Umrah first, then Hajj).
key_terms.مُفْرِد: Mufri, a pilgrim performing the exclusive Hajj (Hajj al-Ifraad).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses 'Arafat and only reaches Jam' before sunrise?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential status of 'Jam'' (the gathering of pilgrims) as the pivotal moment for Hajj validity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Imam's presence and the flexibility of the standing at 'Arafat. It distinguishes between missing the specific ritual of 'Arafat while still in the state of Hajj versus missing the season entirely, prescribing Umrah as the exit mechanism for the former and a full repetition for the latter. The conditional ruling regarding the Imam highlights the significance of following the leader in ritual timing, a key principle in Shia fiqh.
